knowledge.display_text: MCI is an intermediate state between normal cognitive aging and overt dementia, described as slight but noticeable memory and/or other thinking deficits in older adults with minimal impact on daily living.
Some researchers regard MCI as an early dementia stage; cited progression estimates are around 30% annually and 60–90% over a lifetime.

conditions: Cited background claims, not pooled conversion estimates of this prevalence review

knowledge.display_text: Amnestic MCI predominantly affects memory and tends toward AD; nonamnestic MCI affects other thinking skills and may precede frontotemporal/Lewy-body dementia; both may lead to vascular dementia.

statements.modality: seems prodromal for frontotemporal dementia and dementia with Lewy bodies

knowledge.display_text: The source cites a 2016 global annual dementia cost ofUS$315 billion, roughly one quarter of diagnoses in China and a projectedUS$250 billion Chinese burden in 2020 (nearly one fifth of global costs).

attributes.name: author_burden_description
attributes.value: third most serious health problem after cancer and cardio-cerebrovascular disease; burden mostly in low/middle-income countries

knowledge.display_text: Reported MCI prevalence varies by population and method: international ranges 0.5–42% and 6.5–38.6%, China 0.8% versus 20.8%, retired senior cadres 74.23% versus 2.4% in a younger sample; institutional samples should not be pooled indiscriminately with community samples.

conditions: Illustrative cited studies, not this review's pooled estimates

attributes.name: sources_of_variation
attributes.value: age; sampling representativeness; diagnostic criteria; community versus institutional setting

knowledge.display_text: Synthesize MCI and aMCI prevalence for representative community-dwelling older adults in China, with subgroup analyses to inform preventive service planning.
The review followed PRISMA (four-phase flow and 27-item checklist) and registered protocolCRD42019134686 onPROSPERO.
Search ten English/Chinese databases from inception through 1 March 2020, hand-search reference lists and consult a librarian; export to Endnote X9.

attributes.name: databases
attributes.value: Google Scholar; PubMed; Web of Science; Embase; CINAHL; PsycINFO; CQVIP; Wangfang; CNKI; Sinomed

attributes.name: terms
attributes.value: mild cognitive impairment; cognitive dysfunction; early dementia; epidemiology; prevalence; rate; occurrence

knowledge.display_text: Include original population-based cross-sectional/longitudinal community studies with screening plus diagnostic confirmation and representative participants≥55; exclude long-term-care and special disease, occupation, migration, insurance or literacy samples.

conditions: Representative community-based samples; confirmed rather than suspected MCI

attributes.name: age_rationale
attributes.value: no eligible studies under55; no consensus optimal screening start; biological changes can precede dementia by decades; retirement/preventive-care context

attributes.name: excluded_samples
attributes.value: Parkinson disease; depression; stroke; special occupation; internal migration; insurance; literacy; long-term care

knowledge.display_text: Two reviewers screened 2136 deduplicated records;172 full texts yielded 45 eligible studies after 127 exclusions; independent bias assessment with third-person discussion excluded four high-risk studies, leaving 41.
The Risk of Bias Tool graded four external-validity and five internal-validity domains plus overall risk as low, medium or high using a GRADE scheme.

attributes.name: external_domains
attributes.value: target/population representation; sample representation; random sampling; nonresponse bias

attributes.name: internal_domains
attributes.value: data proxy; case definition; instrument validity/reliability; data collection mode; appropriate parameter

knowledge.display_text: Extract MCI/subtype prevalence, urban/rural setting, age, sex, education, living status, period, screening tools and diagnostic methods.

attributes.name: fields
attributes.value: prevalence; urban/rural; age; sex; education; living status; period; screening and confirmation tools

knowledge.display_text: For publication-bias assessment, the methods state that funnel symmetry and Egger tests are used and that p<0.05 indicates absence of publication bias.

conditions: Source wording retained exactly; not silently corrected

attributes.name: test
attributes.value: visual funnel symmetry and Egger test

attributes.name: source_asserted_rule
attributes.value: p below0.05 indicates absence of publication bias

knowledge.display_text: Run random-effects prevalence synthesis in Stata 12, CochranQ/I², leave-one-out sensitivity, subgroup analysis and meta-regression; use two-sidedp<0.05 and 95% confidence intervals.

conditions: Random-effects model; pooled MCI and aMCI separately

attributes.name: sensitivity
attributes.value: sequentially remove each study; exclude significantly deviating studies

knowledge.display_text: The 41 eligible studies comprised 112632 participants, study periods 1998–2020 and prevalence 1.21–33.03%; seven were longitudinal,58% used age>60,75% hadN>1000, and women ranged 25.74–66.89%.
About 30 neuropsychological instruments were used. MMSE/MoCA predominated in screening, ADL assessed daily functioning and CDR helped exclude dementia;25 studies used Petersen confirmation.

conditions: Tools as categorized by the source; no external correction of domain assignments
